transferable_lessons: When a question quotes an exact proper name/challenge title that returns zero hits in SQL LIKE search across all text tables, treat that as a strong signal the memory DB never captured it by name -- pivot search strategy to the surrounding narrative context (e.g. 'boss defeated, collapses into turtle-shell form') rather than repeating name-based queries with more paraphrases.

For questions asking for precise on-screen numeric values (XP amounts, exact levels), do not trust caption/episode text summaries even when they contain a plausible-looking number -- caption text can describe a completely different, semantically similar event (e.g. another level-up screen) elsewhere in a long video. Always clip_qa the specific candidate interval before finalizing.

When multiple semantic_search queries all converge on the same single interval regardless of query phrasing, treat that convergence with suspicion rather than confidence -- it may indicate an attractor/distractor interval that is simply the best available match for a family of related but unindexed events, not proof of correctness.

If clip_qa at a first candidate interval finds no matching visual evidence (no legible reward popup, wrong boss name, etc.), the correct response is to keep searching nearby episode/visual_clips rows for other boss-defeat moments in the same session rather than giving up with a hedge or defaulting to a distant distractor.

For 'defeated X, how much XP and what level' style causal-reasoning questions, first locate ALL boss-defeat / '已击败' moments in the DB (there are many in this 23.6h video) and then use clip_qa to check each nearby one for a legible reward number, since captions rarely index the exact numeric popup.
